filters.name: Compute Obscurance
filters.shortDescription: Computes volumetric obscurance and stores it in quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Compute ambient Obscurance.
Ambient obscurance is a computer graphics technique used to simulate the effect of global ambient light in a 3D scene, making the mesh appear more realistic.
This filter requires two values:
  • the number of rays(defined by the user), which will be shot from the barycenter of each face in order to compute how many time it is visible from these directions;
  • the tau value which represent the T spatial decay;
The resulting values for the obscurance are saved per face, and each vertex takes the average of the values of the faces around it, so both the per-face and the per-vertex scalar are written. The filter does not bake colors; after it runs the view switches to showing the per-face scalar.
This filter uses Embree3 library by INTEL.

parameters.label: Rays
parameters.help: Number of rays shot from each face barycenter.

parameters.label: Tau
parameters.help: Spatial decay factor used in obscurance accumulation.

filters.name: Compute Mesh Ambient Occlusion
filters.shortDescription: Computes cosine-weighted ambient visibility of a surface mesh, per face and per vertex.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Computes self-occlusion on a surface mesh by tracing rays with Intel Embree. Rays start at each face barycenter and only directions in the outward hemisphere contribute, weighted by the cosine of their angle to the face normal. The resulting ambient-visibility scalar is stored per face, and each vertex then takes the average of the values of the faces around it, so both the per-face and the per-vertex scalar are written (replacing any they held); a larger value means that more ambient light reaches the surface. The average unoccluded direction is also stored in the per-face custom attribute `BentNormal`. By default directions cover the sphere uniformly. **Directional Bias** replaces a fraction of them with directions inside the cone defined by **Lighting Direction** and **Cone Half-Angle**: `0` is fully uniform ambient illumination and `1` uses only the cone. More rays improve angular sampling at greater cost. The filter does not bake colors; the view switches to showing the per-face scalar after completion. For a layer without faces use *Compute Point Cloud Ambient Occlusion*.

parameters.label: Rays
parameters.help: Number of lighting directions tested at each face barycenter.

parameters.label: Directional Bias
parameters.help: Fraction of ray directions sampled inside the lighting cone: 0 is uniform ambient light, 1 uses only the cone.

parameters.label: Lighting Direction
parameters.help: Axis of the directionally biased lighting cone.

parameters.label: Cone Half-Angle
parameters.help: Half-angle in degrees of the directionally biased lighting cone.

filters.name: Compute Point Cloud Ambient Occlusion
filters.shortDescription: Computes point-cloud visibility against a surface occluder.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Traces rays from every point of the current point-cloud layer against a separate **Occluder Mesh**, using Intel Embree. The result is stored in vertex quality; a larger value means that the point is more exposed. Layer transforms are respected, and the average direction of escaping rays is stored in the per-vertex custom attribute `BentNormal`. **Normal Source** selects the meaning of the measurement:
  • Point cloud normals computes classical cosine-weighted hemisphere visibility around each existing point normal. Every point must have a valid normal.
  • Closest occluder surface uses the geometric normal of the nearest occluder triangle. This is useful when point normals are absent or noisy and the points sample that surface; it assumes that the occluder orientation is meaningful.
  • No normal (spherical occlusion) tests all sampled directions with equal weight. With Directional Bias set to 0, this is orientation-independent full-sphere accessibility: enclosed points have low values and exposed points have high values. It is not classical hemisphere ambient occlusion. A non-zero directional bias instead measures accessibility under the selected directional distribution.
By default directions cover the sphere uniformly. **Directional Bias** replaces a fraction of them with directions inside the cone defined by **Lighting Direction** and **Cone Half-Angle**: `0` is fully uniform and `1` uses only the cone. More rays improve angular sampling at greater cost. The filter does not bake colors; MeshLab switches to vertex-quality visualization after completion.

parameters.label: Occluder Mesh
parameters.help: Surface mesh tested by rays from the current point cloud.

parameters.label: Normal Source
parameters.help: Selects an existing point normal, the closest occluder triangle normal, or orientation-independent spherical visibility.

parameters.label: Rays
parameters.help: Number of visibility directions tested at each point.

parameters.label: Directional Bias
parameters.help: Fraction of ray directions sampled inside the lighting cone: 0 is uniform ambient light, 1 uses only the cone.

parameters.label: Lighting Direction
parameters.help: Axis of the directionally biased lighting cone.

parameters.label: Cone Half-Angle
parameters.help: Half-angle in degrees of the directionally biased lighting cone.

filters.name: Compute Shape Diameter Function
filters.shortDescription: Computes SDF and stores it in quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Compute Shape-Diameter Function
The SDF defines the distance between a point in 3D space and the nearest point on the object's surface.This filter can be used to find out the thickness of the mesh
Given a face, a set of rays are shot inward, and an average of the distance to hit a face is saved in the face quality. The filter does not bake colors; after it runs MeshLab switches the view to face-quality color visualization.This filter requires two values:
  • the number of rays which will be shot from the barycenter of each face
  • the cone amplitude (in degrees) of the cone which we value as valid for the shooting angle

This filter uses Embree3 library by INTEL.

parameters.label: Rays
parameters.help: Number of rays shot from each face barycenter.

parameters.label: Cone Amplitude
parameters.help: Cone opening angle in degrees used for SDF ray directions.

filters.name: Select Visible Faces
filters.shortDescription: Selects faces visible from a user-defined direction.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Select visible face
This filter displays all visible faces from a given direction, selecting the face is is visible from the point given.This filter utilizes the Embree3 library by INTEL.

filters.name: Orient Face Normals by Ray Casting
filters.shortDescription: Reorients wrongly oriented faces using Embree ray casting.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Reorient face normals by geometry.Given the input mesh, this filter uses raytracing to determine if any faces are pointing inward and corrects their orientation. The number of rays is defined by the user; the higher the number, the higher the precision, but at the cost of computation time.This filter requires two values:
  • the number of rays to be shot from the barycenter of each face
  • Parity Sampling: If selected, the normal analysis will be performed using the Parity Sampling algorithm. It is suggested to use this algotirhm when the standard one (visibility sampling) faild to riorient all faces because it is used to reorient faces invisible from the outside
This filter uses the Embree3 library by Intel.

parameters.label: Rays
parameters.help: Number of rays shot from each face barycenter.

parameters.label: Parity Sampling
parameters.help: Uses parity sampling instead of visibility sampling.
